Let
\[
\beta=m\alpha,\qquad \eta=\frac1m,\qquad q=1-\beta.
\]
Then \(0<\beta\le 2\), \(q\in[-1,1)\), and the three update matrices are
\[
M_k=I-\alpha P_k^{(m)}
=R_k\begin{bmatrix}1-\beta\eta&0\\0&1-\beta\end{bmatrix}R_k^T.
\]
Put
\[
t=1-\beta\eta,\qquad s=1-\beta=q.
\]
The sweep matrix is \(T=M_2M_1M_0\), and \(R_m(\alpha)=\|T\|_2\).

A direct multiplication gives
\[
T=\frac18
\begin{bmatrix}
t(-t^2+6ts+3s^2)&-\sqrt3\,s(t-s)^2\\
\sqrt3\,t(t-s)^2&s(3t^2+6ts-s^2)
\end{bmatrix}.
\]
Thus if \(\lambda\) is the larger eigenvalue of \(T^TT\), then
\[
R_m(\alpha)=\sqrt{\lambda},
\]
where
\[
\lambda=\frac{\tau+\sqrt{\tau^2-4\Delta}}2,
\qquad
\tau=\operatorname{tr}(T^TT),\qquad
\Delta=\det(T)^2=t^6s^6.
\]

At leading order \(\eta=0\), so \(t=1\), \(s=q\). Then
\[
\tau_0(q)=\frac{1-6q+15q^2+12q^3+15q^4-6q^5+q^6}{16}.
\]
The critical equation for the larger eigenvalue reduces to
\[
(q^2-6q+1)(q-1)^6(q+1)^2=0.
\]
The only interior minimizer in \([-1,1)\) is
\[
q_0=3-2\sqrt2,
\]
so
\[
\beta_0=1-q_0=2\sqrt2-2.
\]
At this point
\[
R_\infty=\sqrt{\lambda_0(q_0)}=q_0=3-2\sqrt2.
\]
Hence
\[
A=2\sqrt2-2,\qquad C=3-2\sqrt2.
\]

For the first correction, expand
\[
\lambda(q,\eta)=\lambda_0(q)+\eta\lambda_1(q)+O(\eta^2).
\]
At \(q=q_0\), one obtains
\[
\lambda_0''(q_0)=\frac{3\sqrt2}{2},
\qquad
\lambda_1'(q_0)=132-93\sqrt2,
\qquad
\lambda_1(q_0)=492-348\sqrt2.
\]
Writing
\[
\beta_m=\beta_0+B\eta+o(\eta),
\]
the optimality condition gives
\[
B=\frac{\lambda_1'(q_0)}{\lambda_0''(q_0)}
=-62+44\sqrt2.
\]
Also,
\[
R_m^*
=\sqrt{\lambda_0(q_0)+\eta\lambda_1(q_0)+o(\eta)}
=q_0+\eta\frac{\lambda_1(q_0)}{2q_0}+o(\eta),
\]
so
\[
D=\frac{492-348\sqrt2}{2(3-2\sqrt2)}
=42-30\sqrt2.
\]

Therefore
\[
\boxed{(A,B,C,D)=\left(2\sqrt2-2,\;44\sqrt2-62,\;3-2\sqrt2,\;42-30\sqrt2\right)}.
\]
